name: Surgical technology clinical case requirements
authority: ARC/STSA · CAAHEP (program accreditation) · AST Core Curriculum (case log) · CST exam (NBSTSA)
edition: CAAHEP Standards and Guidelines for the Accreditation of Educational Programs in Surgical Technology, approved June 15, 2023, technical update January 16, 2025 (ARC/STSA), enforcing the Core Curriculum for Surgical Technology 7th edition (CCST-7e) clinical case requirements and role definitions
summary: Every graduate must complete a documented log of a minimum of 120 surgical cases: 30 in General Surgery, at least 20 of them in the First Scrub role and the other 10 in the First or Second Scrub role; 90 in the surgical specialties, at least 60 of them First Scrub across a minimum of four specialties with at least 10 First Scrub cases in each of those four (40) and the other 20 First Scrub cases in any specialty or combination; the remaining 30 specialty cases in the First or Second Scrub role in any specialty. Observation cases are documented but never counted. Up to 10 diagnostic endoscopy cases and up to 5 vaginal delivery cases may count toward the Second Scrub cases (at most 40 of the 120 may be Second Scrub). First Scrub means the student verified supplies and equipment, set up the sterile field with instruments, supplies, equipment, medications and solutions, performed the counts with the circulator before the procedure and before closing, passed instruments and supplies to the sterile team throughout, and maintained sterile technique; Second Scrub means the student was at the sterile field without meeting every First Scrub criterion but actively participated in the whole procedure by sponging, suctioning, cutting suture, holding retractors or manipulating the endoscopic camera and scope; Observation means in the OR in neither role. Cases are counted by the specialty defined in CCST-7e, and every case is verified by the preceptor. Cases are what limit a site: a hospital or ambulatory surgery center takes as many students a day as its case volume supports, and a site only counts toward a specialty if it actually does those procedures.

definitions.first scrub: verified supplies and equipment; set up the sterile field with instruments, supplies, equipment, medications and solutions; performed counts with the circulator before the procedure and before the incision is closed; passed instruments and supplies to the sterile team throughout; maintained sterile technique and corrected breaks
definitions.second scrub: at the sterile field without meeting every First Scrub criterion, actively participating in the procedure in its entirety by sponging, suctioning, cutting suture, holding retractors or manipulating the endoscopic camera and scope
definitions.observation: in the OR in a role that meets neither First nor Second Scrub — documented, not counted
